MESSAGE.value: Package shuffling, part 1
Final bit of package shuffling. (Dunno why svn was such a PITA...)
When calculating the latest time for mincha, I realized that adding the 25 seconds could cause a rounding issue. In order to avoid any problems, I'm only going to add the 13 minutes.
Add logic for figuring out when we should show candle lighting or havdalah times.

Add support for swiping to change the day being displayed. When you swipe: * left-to-right: move to the previous day * right-to-left: move to the next day * top-to-bottom: move to the previous month * bottom-to-top: move to the next month
Update to use Android 1.6
Adding icu4j library.
Tried to update HebrewDateUtils to do everything needed, realized I needed something more professional. Including initial commit of icu4j classes (http://site.icu-project.org/)
Tried to update HebrewDateUtils to do everything needed, realized I needed something more professional. Will be moving to icu4j...

Adding svn:ignore on the bin directory, generated by the ant build script.

Used android tool to generate ant files. Added svn:ignore so the generated bin directory doesn't show up.
Get the correct location using the coarse location permission.
Start copying ICU classes that we need.
Sucking in icu4j. Will be making minor mods to make it play nicely with Android.

A few mods to ICU4J so that it will play more nicely with Android. * Basically, the ICUAndroidBridge class can be used now, if an instance has been previously created. It will use the AssetManager to load things. * We're not yet using the HebrewCalendar, but I've verified in the debugger that it DOES work!!!
NOTES: * Loading the hebrewDateFormatter [= com.ibm.icu.text.DateFormat.getDateInstance(...)] still causes some fatal exception(s) to be thrown. * Currently, I've copied the _entire_ contents of the icudata.jar into my assets directory. This is horrible, as it causes the .apk to be 7.7MB. And, I KNOW that the vast majority of those resource files are not necessary.
Chanukah is 8 days. (Not that it really matters yet...the DateRule in use won't handle multi-day holidays...)
